description: Get the current signed-in user's profile information
examples: Who am I signed in as?
notes: The /me endpoint is an alias for /users/{signed-in-user-id}. Only requires User.Read scope. Some properties like employeeId, onPremisesExtensionAttributes may require User.Read.All.

description: Get a specific user's profile by user ID or user principal name (UPN/email)
examples: Get the profile for this user
notes: The {user_id_or_upn} can be a user GUID or a userPrincipalName (typically the email address). Requires User.Read.All (delegated) or User.Read.All (application). For guest users, use their full UPN which may differ from their email.

description: Search for users by display name
examples: Search for a user named John Smith
Find users with 'Sarah' in their name
Who is John in the directory?
notes: Use startsWith() for prefix matching on displayName. For broader search, use $search="displayName:John" with the ConsistencyLevel=eventual header and $count=true. The $search approach supports partial matching but requires additional headers.

Returns a directoryObject that is typically a user. If no manager is set, returns 404 Not Found. The response @odata.type will be #microsoft.graph.user. Can also use /users/{id}/manager to get another user's manager.

description: Get the current user's direct reports
notes: Returns directoryObjects that are typically users. If the user has no direct reports, returns an empty collection. Can also use /users/{id}/directReports for another user's reports.

description: List the groups and directory roles the current user is a member of
examples: Show me the teams and groups I belong to
What groups is my account a member of?
notes: Returns a mix of groups, directory roles, and administrative units. Filter by @odata.type to get only groups: /me/memberOf/microsoft.graph.group. The results include Microsoft 365 groups, security groups, distribution lists, and directory roles.

examples: Get the avatar for this user
notes: Returns the binary image data of the user's profile photo. Response Content-Type is typically image/jpeg. Returns 404 if no photo is set. For another user's photo, use /users/{id}/photo/$value (requires User.Read.All). Use /me/photo for metadata (size, width, height) without the binary content.

description: List users in the organization's directory
examples: List all users in the organization
notes: Returns paginated results. Use $top and @odata.nextLink for paging. Filter by accountEnabled to exclude disabled accounts. For large directories, consider using $filter or $search to narrow results. Maximum $top value is 999.

description: Get another user's manager by user ID or UPN
examples: Show me the manager of this user
notes: Returns the specified user's manager as a directoryObject. Returns 404 if no manager is assigned. The {user_id_or_upn} can be a GUID or email/UPN.

description: Get another user's direct reports by user ID or UPN
examples: List the team under this manager
notes: Returns the specified user's direct reports. Returns an empty collection if they have no reports. Useful for building org chart views.
